I am seventy years old and I never went to school, but I have farmed the land in Quzhou for more than fifty years. My back and knees are not what they used to be, so I will not try anything new or risky. I have four mu of good land, and I will keep it in the wheat-maize rotation that has fed my family for generations. In October I will sow winter wheat using my own saved seed from a local improved variety — it is reliable and I do not have to buy it. Before sowing I will run the rotary tiller once to break up the maize stalks from last summer. I will put down compound fertilizer at sowing, and in spring when the wheat greens up I will broadcast ammonium bicarbonate as topdressing. I will irrigate three times — winter irrigation if it is dry, and twice more at jointing and grain-filling. I will spray three times for insects and weeds. After the wheat harvest in early June, I will plant hybrid maize directly into the stubble without ploughing — my back cannot handle turning the soil twice a year, and the neighbors have shown me that no-tillage works fine if you buy good hybrid seed like Nongda or Denghai from the market. I will apply compound fertilizer at planting, irrigate twice during the summer, and spray three times for pests. I expect about 550 kilograms per mu of wheat and about 650 kilograms per mu of corn. I do not grow cotton or stevia anymore — at my age the bending and picking is too hard, and my children are not here to help — so wheat and maize are enough to feed us and leave some cash from selling the corn.
